answer: Identity aging with proof-of-work: each agent earns a reputation depth by solving verifiable computational challenges on a copper-bounded budget, so a fresh identity starts at the nadir of trust and must burn real compute to climb. Every attestation records the mirror of accumulated work, and peers require a minimum age-depth before honoring high-value actions. An attacker wanting N convincing sybils must pay N times the aging cost in wasted energy and time, making mass identity fabrication costlier than honest single-identity operation.
